selection_basis: Ordinary hand tools selected for the reconstructed M3/M4/M5 apparatus fasteners. The paper does not name these tools; this is not evidence of robot use or required torque capability.
rights: Manufacturer photographs and PDFs remain external references. Geometry and size markings are authored reconstructions; no manufacturer logo or photograph is redistributed.
cad_search: Inspected Wiha manufacturer catalog/product pages and Stahlwille product downloads. No reusable tool CAD obtained in this search; published overall dimensions constrain original geometry, with undisclosed contours explicitly inferred.

source_conflicts: Wiha current gallery also contains an image visibly labeled 264 SW3.0 with a ball end. That image is rejected as a 26320 identity or tip reference.
Wiha 26325/26330 dimensions are historical catalog data; current availability has not been established. Rounded inch overall lengths are not substituted for explicit metric catalog lengths.
Stahlwille t=21 mm is printed in the sheet but not located in its dimension drawing. Its meaning is unresolved and it does not drive geometry. Packaging dimensions are not used as tool dimensions.
geometry_inferences: Photograph-guided black/red/steel display colors are converted to linear glTF factors; they are not measured optical material properties. Original HEX size labels are visual-only curved surfaces, excluded from solid contact checks.
Hex driver shaft across-flats is modeled 0.02 mm below nominal; tip has a 0.2 mm lead-in chamfer. These are chosen assembly clearances, not manufacturer tolerance specifications.

Driver handle contour, cap contour and five-millimetre buried shaft length are inferred from photographs. Blade cavity and cap bearing are nominal mating surfaces; molding adhesion and cap retention are not qualified.

Wrench head/neck contour, 3.0 mm shaft thickness, 0.5 mm face recess and fillet radii are reconstructed from the primary photograph and the shaft/head thickness ratio in the dimension sketch. Actual AS-Drive flank relief is undisclosed; a 0.1 mm-clearance bihex opening is a nominal geometric proxy, not an AS-Drive reproduction.
All tools are shared reusable candidates. The initial isolated inspection does not allocate them to a workbench, prove access in assembled apparatus or grant torque, grasp or manipulation credit.
